z-m-15-05.title: Which graph good to show same data?
z-m-15-05.goal: Compare wetin each kind graph show well and poorly, then choose graph wey fit purpose and give reason.
z-m-15-05.material:
School library survey number of books borrowed each month from March to August.
March 350, April 380, May 420, June 300, July 410, August 560 (6-month total 2420)
We want show data in graph. For pie chart, no write book counts or total, only sector sizes and month names, and arrange sectors from biggest.
z-m-15-05.thinking.0: Compare and evaluate ways to show data for a purpose
z-m-15-05.thinking.1: Distinguish wetin graph show from wetin e hide
z-m-15-05.thinking.2: Accept say more than one choice fit valid
z-m-15-05.prereq.0: Can read line graphs and bar graphs (Primary 4 level)
z-m-15-05.prereq.1: Know circle graph or band graph show part-to-whole ratios (Primary 6 level)
z-m-15-05.s.s1.prompt: You want show at a glance how borrowed books from March to August change (up and down pattern). Which graph best?
z-m-15-05.s.s1.hint.0: In one sentence say whether you want show “how many each month” or “how e change as months pass.”
z-m-15-05.s.s1.hint.1: Picture each graph and compare whether May-to-June change stand out.
z-m-15-05.s.s1.r.a: Dis graph show each month share of total. E no fit well show rising and falling pattern as months pass.
z-m-15-05.s.s1.r.b: E good for comparing each month sizes. For trend, line graph fit better.
z-m-15-05.s.s1.r.c: Dis graph put whole into one strip to show shares. E hard to show which way things change over months.
z-m-15-05.s.s1.r.d: You remember say na graph wey show quantity changing over time with line rising and falling.
z-m-15-05.s.s1.explain: To show how values change over time, line graph direct pass. Bar graph fit compare months too, but line graph show upward/downward movement clearer as line connect.
z-m-15-05.s.s1.acc.0: Bar graph easy too for month-to-month comparison, and you fit read ups and downs from bar height. But line graph slope show direction and size of change clearer at glance.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.prompt: When you draw pie chart (no book counts or total, only sector sizes and month names, sectors arranged biggest first), choose all things you fit tell straight from graph.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.hint.0: First sort out whether circle graph show “number of books” or “share of whole.”
z-m-15-05.s.s2.hint.1: Put each question into ones share can answer and ones needing order or change amount.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.o.a: About what percent of all 6 months August borrowing be
z-m-15-05.s.s2.r.a: Looking at share one sector take of whole na feature of circle graph.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.o.b: By how many books borrowing drop between May and June
z-m-15-05.s.s2.r.b: Sectors show only share, and book count and total no dey written. From graph alone you no fit tell how many books e drop.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.o.c: Month with most borrowing among 6 months
z-m-15-05.s.s2.r.c: You fit find am by looking for biggest sector.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.o.d: Whether borrowing keep rising across 6 months
z-m-15-05.s.s2.r.d: Sectors arrange from biggest, so month order no dey. Without order, e hard to know ups and downs over time.
z-m-15-05.s.s2.explain: For pie chart, you fit tell shares and biggest item from sector sizes. August na 560÷2420, about 23%. But since book counts no dey written and month order unknown, pie chart alone no show how many books e drop or whether e increase over time.
z-m-15-05.s.s3.prompt: Friend wey draw circle graph talk, “Just by looking this graph, you fit fully see how borrowing dey go up.” Write your view to friend, including wetin circle graph show well and wetin e no show well.
z-m-15-05.s.s3.hint.0: First write one thing you fit read from sector sizes in circle graph.
z-m-15-05.s.s3.hint.1: Then write one thing line graph of same data show, but wey hard to read from circle graph.
z-m-15-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you write both wetin person fit know and wetin hard to know from circle graph?
z-m-15-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Is there example (like August share) to support your view?
z-m-15-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did you connect am to situations wey need line graph or another graph?
z-m-15-05.s.s3.model.0: Circle graph show well percentage each month take of whole. For example, August get biggest sector. But ups and downs as months pass hard to see, so line graph better to show trend.
z-m-15-05.s.s3.model.1: Circle graph show say August biggest, about 23% of whole. But June drop and July rise again hard to notice because month order and book count no dey.
z-m-15-05.s.s3.modelNote.1: E go even better to add hint say things fit change if number of books dey written too.

z-m-15-04.title: Di bag wey get more red marbles better?
z-m-15-04.topic: Compare chances (two cases with different totals)
z-m-15-04.goal: Decide what information you need to compare chances, revise your comparison when new information show, and make example to show say “more” and “more likely” no be the same.
z-m-15-04.material: Bags 가 and 나 dey. Close your eyes and take one marble from each bag. Marbles differ only by color; size and shape same. You win if you pick red marble. Pick only once and no put am back.
z-m-15-04.prereq.0: Express one part of whole as fraction
z-m-15-04.prereq.1: Compare fractions with different denominators (Primary 5–6 level)
z-m-15-04.s.s1.prompt: All we know now na “bag 가 get 3 red marbles and bag 나 get 5 red marbles.” Wetin most suitable thing to say about which bag give better chance to win?
z-m-15-04.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine wetin fit happen if there be 100 other marbles even though red ones na 3.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.hint.1: Give one example of how chance change when number of marbles in other colors change, even if red marble number stay same.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.o.a: Bag 나 get better chance. E get 2 more red marbles.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.r.a: You compare only number of red marbles. We no know yet what share of all marbles dey red.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.o.b: Bag 가 get better chance. Di fewer marbles bag get, di easier to pick red.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.r.b: You assume total marbles small, but we no get that information. Na guess without evidence.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.o.c: We no fit compare unless we know total marbles (or number of marbles with other colors).
z-m-15-04.s.s1.r.c: You point out say chance depend on red marble number and total marble number together.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.o.d: Red fit come out or no come out, so both chances same.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.r.d: You judge chances same just because two outcomes dey. Same number of outcomes no mean same chances.
z-m-15-04.s.s1.explain: Chance na share of all marbles wey red marbles take. If na only red marble number we know, we no know total, so we no fit say which chance higher. For situation like dis, first talk “wetin more we need to know.”
z-m-15-04.s.s2.prompt: New information don come. Bag 가 get 2 blue marbles and bag 나 get 4 blue marbles, and no other colors dey in either bag. Now which bag get higher chance to win?
z-m-15-04.s.s2.hint.0: First find total number of marbles in each bag.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.hint.1: Write both chances as fractions, make denominators same, then compare.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.o.a: Bag 가 higher. Red marbles be bigger share of all marbles.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.r.a: Dis judgment compare as fractions what part of whole red marbles be in both bags.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.o.b: Bag 나 higher. E get more red marbles, 5.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.r.b: Even with new information, you compare only red marble number. Check whether total marble number don change.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.o.c: Both bags same. Each one get 1 more red marble than blue marble.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.r.c: You think say if difference between red and blue counts same, chances same. Even if difference same, totals differ, so shares fit differ.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.o.d: Total marbles differ, so even after calculating we no fit compare.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.r.d: You think we no fit compare when denominators differ. We fit make denominators same or change to decimals.
z-m-15-04.s.s2.explain: Bag 가 get 3 red out of 5 total, na 3/5 (0.6); bag 나 get 5 red out of 9, na 5/9 (about 0.56). With denominator 45 dem become 27/45 and 25/45, so bag 가 small higher. Even though bag 나 get more red marbles, bag 가 get higher chance to win.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.prompt: Make your own case wey claim “bag with more red marbles always get higher chance to win” no hold. Write red marble numbers and total marbles for both bags, and explain why.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.hint.0: First put very small number of red marbles and small total for one bag.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.hint.1: Make di other bag get plenty red marbles but even more marbles in other colors, then compare chances as fractions.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.placeholder: For example: Bag A get ... red marbles out of ... total.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did di bag with more red marbles get lower chance to win?
z-m-15-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you compare both bags’ chances in di same way and show numbers?
z-m-15-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did you explain with your example how “more marbles” differ from “higher chance”?
z-m-15-04.s.s3.model.0: Bag 가 get 4 red and 1 blue, 5 total; bag 나 get 6 red and 6 blue, 12 total. Bag 나 get more red marbles, but 가 get 4 out of 5 and 나 6 out of 12, so 가 chance higher.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.model.1: Bag A get 3 red out of 10, na 3/10; bag B get 1 red out of 1, so win certain. Even though A get more red marbles, B chance higher.
z-m-15-04.s.s3.modelNote.1: E extreme example, but e satisfy condition.

z-m-15-07.thinking.0: Test one general idea with counterexample
z-m-15-07.prereq.0: Know what mean be and find mean of simple data (Grade 5-6)
z-m-15-07.title: Fit more students receive allowance wey pass the average?
z-m-15-07.topic: The difference between the mean and individual data
z-m-15-07.goal: Show with counterexample say even with the same mean, most data values fit fall below the mean, and talk when e make sense to use the mean as representative value.
z-m-15-07.material: The mean monthly allowance for a group of 5 people na 5천 원. Allowances na whole numbers in units of 1천 원, and all 5 people get at least 1천 원. If dem write allowance in units of '천 원,' the total allowance for the 5 people na 25 (천 원), and the mean na 5 (천 원).
z-m-15-07.thinking.1: Making different data sets wey meet one condition
z-m-15-07.thinking.2: Explaining the uses and limits of a representative value
z-m-15-07.prereq.1: Sums and size comparison of natural numbers
z-m-15-07.s.s1.prompt: To show say the idea 'The mean na 5천 원, so most of the 5 people must get at least 5천 원' fit wrong, which kind case you suppose look for?
z-m-15-07.s.s1.hint.0: First write how many 천 원 you go get when you add the allowances for all 5 people if the mean na 5천 원.
z-m-15-07.s.s1.hint.1: Think about wetin go happen to the other 4 people's total if one person get far more than the mean.
z-m-15-07.s.s1.o.a: A case wey all 5 people get exactly 5천 원 each
z-m-15-07.s.s1.r.a: If everybody get 5천 원, all 5 people get at least 5천 원, so e no oppose that idea.
z-m-15-07.s.s1.o.b: A case wey nobody get less than 5천 원
z-m-15-07.s.s1.r.b: If nobody get less than the mean, everybody get at least 5천 원, so e support that idea.
z-m-15-07.s.s1.o.c: A case wey total allowance for the 5 people pass 25 (천 원)
z-m-15-07.s.s1.r.c: If the total no be 25 (천 원), the mean no be 5천 원. You must keep the condition say the mean na 5천 원.
z-m-15-07.s.s1.o.d: A case wey only 1 person get at least 5천 원
z-m-15-07.s.s1.r.d: This judgment remember a case wey one person get plenty and the others get less than the mean, so the total still be 25 (천 원).
z-m-15-07.s.s1.explain: As long as the total na 25 (천 원), the mean na 5 (천 원). For example, with 3, 3, 3, 4, 12 (천 원), the total na 25 and mean na 5, but na only the 1 person wey get 12천 원 get at least 5천 원. If even one case like this dey, the idea 'The mean na 5천 원, so most people get at least 5천 원' no always correct.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different sets of allowances for 5 people (in units of 천 원) where the mean for the 5 people na 5천 원 and exactly 1 person get at least 5천 원. (Cases wey only change the order count as the same case.)
z-m-15-07.s.s2.hint.0: Choose one person wey get at least 5천 원, and put each of the other 4 people at 4천 원 or below.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.hint.1: Once you set the total for the other 4 people, check say the one person's allowance na 25 minus that total.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.ok.c1: All of dem na whole numbers wey be at least 1.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Every allowance must be whole number wey be at least 1천 원 (in units of 천 원).
z-m-15-07.s.s2.ok.c2: The total na 25 (천 원), so the mean na 5천 원.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.fail.c2: The total for the 5 people no be 25 (천 원).
z-m-15-07.s.s2.ok.c3: Exactly 1 person get at least 5천 원.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.fail.c3: E no be exactly 1 person wey get at least 5천 원.
z-m-15-07.s.s2.explain: If the other 4 people all get 4천 원 or less, their total no fit pass 16 (천 원), so the 1 person must get at least 9천 원. Plenty cases dey, like 3, 3, 3, 4, 12 or 4, 4, 4, 4, 9. Even with the same mean, individual data fit different like this.
z-m-15-07.s.s3.prompt: Use the examples wey you make above explain why the saying 'The mean na 5천 원, so our friends for this group probably get about 5천 원 each' fit no be correct, and write when e okay to use the mean as representative value for this group.
z-m-15-07.s.s3.hint.0: Write the exact numbers for one of the examples wey you make above.
z-m-15-07.s.s3.hint.1: For the other side, think how the mean go feel if all 5 people get between 4천 원 and 6천 원.
z-m-15-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You use the numbers for your example show say 'most people get less than the mean'?
z-m-15-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You state at least one condition wey the mean fit serve as representative value?
z-m-15-07.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You show the different uses without declaring say the mean useless?
z-m-15-07.s.s3.model.0: If one person get plenty, the mean go rise, and the others go get less than the mean. For example, with 3, 3, 3, 4, 12천 원, the mean na 5천 원 but 4 people get less than 5천 원. When people's allowances dey close to one another, e okay to use the mean as representative value.
z-m-15-07.s.s3.model.1: If one data value much bigger pass the others, the mean dey pull toward that value and e differ from most values. If the values gather close together, the mean na suitable representative value.
z-m-15-07.s.s3.modelNote.1: E no get example numbers, but the reason and condition clear.

z-m-15-08.title: Making rules for card game with different chances to win
z-m-15-08.goal: Check whether rules overlap, design your own game rules wey meet the conditions, and write each player's chance to win as fraction, confirming say many designs dey possible.
z-m-15-08.material: There are 20 cards, each with one number from 1 to 20 written on it. Shuffle all the cards, put dem face down, and draw one. Every card get equal chance to come out. A and B play game: A win if a 'multiple of m' come out, and B win if a 'multiple of n' come out. (m and n na different natural numbers from 2 to 20, and the players choose the values of m and n.)
z-m-15-08.thinking.0: Finding unclear points for the rules
z-m-15-08.thinking.2: Writing chances as fractions and comparing dem
z-m-15-08.prereq.0: Knows multiples and fit find multiples up to 20 (grade 5 level)
z-m-15-08.prereq.1: Expressing part of a whole as fraction (grades 5-6 level)
z-m-15-08.s.s1.prompt: First, we try rule say A wins if multiple of 4 come out and B wins if multiple of 6 come out. Wetin be the first problem to solve for this rule?
z-m-15-08.s.s1.hint.0: Write all the cards wey A fit win with and all the cards wey B fit win with, then put the lists side by side.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.hint.1: Look for any number wey dey inside both lists.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.o.a: There are more multiples of 4 than 6, so B no fit win at all.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.r.a: The multiples of 6, wey be 6, 12, and 18, dey among the cards, so B fit win too. List the cards each person fit win with by yourself.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.o.b: If 12 come out, both A and B win, so we no fit decide who win.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.r.b: You point out say one card fit both rules, so the rules overlap.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.o.c: There are 20 cards, so we no fit play game with multiples.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.r.c: You connect the number of cards to whether the game fit play. Even with 20 cards, we fit use rule with multiples.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.o.d: A and B chances to win must be equal, so we must use the same number instead of 4 and 6.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.r.d: If you use the same number, both players go always win together. Fairness and no overlap na different problems.
z-m-15-08.s.s1.explain: The multiples of 4 are the 5 cards 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and multiples of 6 are the 3 cards 6, 12, 18. 12 apply to both players, so if 12 come out we no fit decide the winner. First we must check say no such overlap dey.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different rules (m, n) wey meet all these conditions. Conditions: ① No card make both players win at the same time. ② A chance to win higher pass B chance. ③ B chance to win still at least 2 out of 20.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.hint.0: List the cards wey be multiples of m and the cards wey be multiples of n, and check say no number dey in common.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.hint.1: First choose how many cards A go get, then try n one after the other so B number of cards go at least 2 and less than A own.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.var.m: The multiple m wey A wins with
z-m-15-08.s.s2.var.n: The multiple n wey B wins with
z-m-15-08.s.s2.ok.c1: m and n na different natural numbers from 2 to 20.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.fail.c1: m and n must be different natural numbers from 2 to 20.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.ok.c2: No card make both players win at the same time.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.fail.c2: There is common multiple of m and n between 1 and 20, so one card go make both players win at the same time.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.ok.c3: A get more cards wey A fit win with than B.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.fail.c3: A chance to win no higher than B own.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.ok.c4: B get at least 2 cards wey B fit win with.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.fail.c4: B get fewer than 2 cards wey B fit win with.
z-m-15-08.s.s2.explain: For no card to overlap, the common multiples of m and n must pass 20, and you fit count the cards as the quotient (rounded down) of 20÷m. For example, with (3, 7), A get the 6 cards 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 (6 out of 20), and B get the 2 cards 7, 14 (2 out of 20). Plenty rules dey possible, like (4, 7), (5, 6), (6, 10).
z-m-15-08.s.s3.prompt: Choose one of the rules wey you just make, write A and B chances to win each as fraction, and explain how you check say no card make both players win at the same time.
z-m-15-08.s.s3.hint.0: Write all A cards and all B cards for the rule wey you choose.
z-m-15-08.s.s3.hint.1: Write in one sentence how you compare the two lists.
z-m-15-08.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You write the two chances based on the same whole (20 cards)?
z-m-15-08.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You talk say you check for no overlap with method like lists or common multiples?
z-m-15-08.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You check again say your rule meet all conditions ①, ②, ③?
z-m-15-08.s.s3.model.0: My rule na say A wins on multiples of 3 and B wins on multiples of 7. A get the 6 cards 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, so na 6 out of 20, and B get the 2 cards 7, 14, so na 2 out of 20. The common multiples of 3 and 7 start from 21, so no overlapping card dey between 1 and 20.
z-m-15-08.s.s3.model.1: A get 5 cards wey be multiples of 4, so na 5/20, and B get 2 cards wey be multiples of 7, so na 2/20. I write all multiples of 4 and 7 and no same card dey, so no case dey wey both win at once.
z-m-15-08.s.s3.modelNote.1: Na method wey check by writing the lists directly.

z-m-15-01.title: Wetin happen to mean wen one more record added?
z-m-15-01.topic: Change in mean (wen one more data value added)
z-m-15-01.goal: First judge how mean change wen one new data value added, then find different values wey give target mean range, testing your idea with numbers.
z-m-15-01.material: Basketball club play 5 games. Points for each game na 8, 12, 9, 15 and 11. Points for one game na whole number (no decimal or fraction) from 0 to 25. After 6th game, dem find new '6-game mean score'. (Mean score na total points divided by number of games.)
z-m-15-01.thinking.0: Reason how new value connect to mean
z-m-15-01.thinking.1: Find different values wey meet one condition
z-m-15-01.thinking.2: Use numbers show say wrong intuition wrong
z-m-15-01.prereq.0: Know what mean be and find mean of simple data (Grade 5-6)
z-m-15-01.prereq.1: Four arithmetic operations with natural numbers
z-m-15-01.s.s1.prompt: Mean score for first 5 games na 11 points. If club score 12 points in 6th game (1 point above current mean), wetin happen to mean for 6 games?
z-m-15-01.s.s1.hint.0: First check say mean of first 5 games really na 11 points.
z-m-15-01.s.s1.hint.1: Make 6th game score 12 points and find mean for all 6 games directly.
z-m-15-01.s.s1.o.a: E become 12 points, so mean increase by 1 point
z-m-15-01.s.s1.r.a: You treat new score like say na mean. Think say first 5 game scores dey inside mean too.
z-m-15-01.s.s1.o.b: E become above 11 but below 12 points
z-m-15-01.s.s1.r.b: Na judgment wey see say new score above mean go raise mean, but because game number increase, mean no reach new score.
z-m-15-01.s.s1.o.c: Only game count increase, so mean stay 11 even though score higher
z-m-15-01.s.s1.r.c: You think adding game score above mean leave mean same. Think how total change.
z-m-15-01.s.s1.o.d: Game number increase to 6, so mean go below 11
z-m-15-01.s.s1.r.d: You only look game count increasing, no think about size of new score. Wetin matter be whether added score higher or lower than mean.
z-m-15-01.s.s1.explain: Total for first 5 games na 55, and add 12 make 67. 67÷6 na about 11.17, higher than 11 but below 12. If new score above mean, mean increase, but as number of games increase, mean no reach the new score.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.prompt: Try 3 different x values, 6th game score, so 6-game mean dey from 12 to 13 points.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.hint.0: Write expression for total of 6 games if 6th score na x points.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.hint.1: Think backward: wetin total must be for mean to be 12? Then find smallest value x fit be.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.ok.c1: Na whole number from 0 to 25 points.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Score must be whole number from 0 to 25 points.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.ok.c2: Mean for 6 games at least 12 points.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Mean for 6 games at most 13 points.
z-m-15-01.s.s2.explain: For mean to be 12, total for 6 games must be 72 points; for 13, total must be 78. Since first 5 total 55, x na whole number from 17 to 23. All 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 possible.

z-m-15-03.title: If percentages on graph total 101%, e wrong?
z-m-15-03.goal: Explain say rounded percentages fit fail to total 100%, then make cases yourself and talk wetin to watch out for wen reading graph.
z-m-15-03.material: 40 people answer, 'Which one book you wan read first?' Each choose only one: novel, science or comics. One group write pie chart: novel 33%, science 33%, comics 35%, but total na 101%. Each percentage na (number of people wey choose item)÷40×100 rounded to nearest whole number at first decimal place. (Round up if digit na 5 or more.)
z-m-15-03.thinking.0: Reason about possible causes wen result look odd
z-m-15-03.thinking.2: Explain limits of one way to display data
z-m-15-03.prereq.0: Express part of whole as percentage (Grade 6 level)
z-m-15-03.prereq.1: Round to first decimal place (Grade 5 level)
z-m-15-03.s.s1.prompt: Total na 101%. Wetin most suitable thing to talk about this graph?
z-m-15-03.s.s1.hint.0: Work backward one by one to see how many of the 40 people match 33%, 33% and 35%.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether number of people you find total 40, and write exact percentages before rounding.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.o.a: Because each percentage rounded, total fit no be 100%
z-m-15-03.s.s1.r.a: You notice condition say written values approximate. Checking with real people counts make reasoning stronger.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.o.b: Percentages must always total exactly 100%, so one calculation wrong somewhere
z-m-15-03.s.s1.r.b: You treat total of approximate numbers same as total of exact numbers. Think separately about exact and rounded values.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.r.c: You read total percentage as number of people. Whole group na 40 people, so find another reason why total pass 100%.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.o.d: For circle graph, no need to check total percentages.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.r.d: You skip checking total completely. When total look strange, e important to find reason.
z-m-15-03.s.s1.explain: If each percentage na rounded value, even exact values wey add to 100% fit round to different total. For dis data, if people numbers na 13, 13, and 14, exact percentages na 32.5%, 32.5%, and 35%; rounding give 33%, 33%, and 35%. You no fit know without people numbers, so check actual numbers.
z-m-15-03.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different cases apart from 13, 13, 14 above, where people wey choose a, b, c add to 40 but rounded percentages no add to 100%. (Each group get at least 1 person.)

Out of 40, one person na 2.5%, so if two choices get odd number of people, .5 round up twice and total become 101%. If all numbers even, total na 100%.

z-m-15-06.title: Forecast say 70% chance of rain, but rain no fall
z-m-15-06.goal: Distinguish one-day result from records over many days, revise your judgment about chance and confidence as data grow, and design records you need to judge.
z-m-15-06.material: Weather forecast say, “Tomorrow chance of rain na 70%.” Here 70% chance mean “70% of di way between no rain at all (0%) and rain for sure (100%).” We want use records to think how trustworthy forecast be.
z-m-15-06.thinking.0: Revise judgment and confidence according to amount of data
z-m-15-06.thinking.1: Distinguish one result from records across many tries
z-m-15-06.thinking.2: Decide for yourself what data judgment need
z-m-15-06.prereq.0: Experience expressing chance as number from 0 to 100%
z-m-15-06.prereq.1: Relation between percentages and fractions (Primary 6 level)
z-m-15-06.s.s1.prompt: Dem reveal data one piece at a time. Each time choose how you go judge forecast.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.hint.0: At each stage, calculate rainy days divided by total days yourself, then compare with 70%.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.hint.1: As records grow, sort out which first judgments to keep and which to change.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.info: Day after forecast, rain no fall.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.ask: How you fit judge forecast from only this one-day result?
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.after: 70% chance mean 30% chance say rain may not fall. From one day result, e hard to judge whether forecast right or wrong.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Forecast wrong. E say 70% and rain no fall, so forecast no correct.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You read 70% as “rain go surely fall.” Di 30% chance na chance say e no go rain.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.o.b: E hard to call am wrong from one day result alone. Chance of no rain na 30% too.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Dis judgment no decide chance from one result; e also consider remaining chance.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Forecast correct. Chance of no rain reach 30%, so result match forecast.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You call am “correct” because rain no fall. From one result e hard even to tell whether forecast correct.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.o.d: If rain chance na 70%, rain must fall, so if e no rain, forecast agency make mistake.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You treat 70% same as 100%. 70% no mean “for sure.”
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.info: We collect 10 days when same forecaster say “70% chance of rain.” Rain fall on 7 days and no fall on 3.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.ask: Looking at dis record, how you go judge dis forecaster 70% forecasts?
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.after: 7 days out of 10 match 70% well. But 10 days small, so more records fit make your confidence stronger. Dis record give much better evidence than one result.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Record match 70% well, but 10 days no plenty, so we should collect more.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You consider both say record no conflict with forecast and say data amount still small.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Record no conflict with forecast, so we fit trust dis forecaster 70%.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You trust am more because record match forecast. Better still to consider say na only 10 days.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.o.c: E no rain for 3 days, so this forecaster make wrong forecast.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You count every day wey no rain as 'wrong forecast.' 70% still mean say e fit no rain for about 3 days.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.1.o.d: With 70%, rain must fall for all 10 days before the forecast go correct.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.info: We gather the first 10 days wey another forecaster talk say '70%,' and rain fall for 2 days. After we gather 40 more days, we get 50 days altogether, and rain fall for 16 days altogether.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.ask: How you go judge this forecaster 70% forecasts?
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.after: 16 days out of 50 na 32%. From the records of days wey dem forecast 70%, e far from 70%. As the records dey increase, the explanation say the first result na coincidence dey lose strength, and your judgment dey move toward say this forecaster 70% hard to trust as e be.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.o.a: 50 days still small and na chance only, so we fit continue to trust the 70% forecast.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Even though the data reach 50 days, you try hold on to your first belief. Look the pattern wey the bigger data dey show.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.o.b: We no need any more records; we fit decide say this forecaster forecasts don already fail.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You see say records for 50 days na clear clue, but you block the possibility say new data fit come later.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.o.c: We no fit know the weather for each day, so records wey dem gather for many days no get use.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You throw away the clue wey records for many days dey give. Even if you no fit know one day, you fit talk about the pattern across many days.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.o.d: 16÷50 na 32%, wey far from 70%, so e hard to trust the 70% as e be.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.st.2.r.d: This judgment find the proportion of rainy days for the record and compare am with the forecast chance.
z-m-15-06.s.s1.reflect: Each time you look the result for one day, the 10-day record, and the 50-day record, how your judgment about 'This forecast trustworthy?' and how sure you be change? For which point your certainty change pass?
